steps: Drain the soaked rajma and pressure cook it in about 200 ml water a person with a pinch of the salt, on medium-high for 15 to 20 minutes.
Let the pressure drop on its own and check a bean: it should mash easily. If not, cook it a few minutes more.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium heat and add the cumin. Let it sizzle until it browns.
Add the onion and fry for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until golden brown.
Turn the heat to low, add the ginger, garlic and green chilli and stir for about a minute, until the raw smell goes.
Add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and garam masala and cook on medium-low for 10 to 15 minutes, until oil shows.
Add the rajma with its cooking water and the rest of the salt and simmer on low for 15 to 20 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken it.
Stir in the crushed kasuri methi, the ghee and the coriander leaves, turn off the heat and serve with rice.
note: Sources used 40 to 60 g of dry rajma a serving, and 50 g is the middle. Cream is optional in every source and is left out; one source cooks in butter, so oil with a spoon of ghee is used instead.
